From eb7024bfcc5f68ed11ed9dd4891a3073c15f04a8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Varun R Mallya <varunrmallya@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 00:41:25 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Reject sleepable kprobe_multi programs at attach time

kprobe.multi programs run in atomic/RCU context and cannot sleep.
However, bpf_kprobe_multi_link_attach() did not validate whether the
program being attached had the sleepable flag set, allowing sleepable
helpers such as bpf_copy_from_user() to be invoked from a non-sleepable
context.

This causes a "sleeping function called from invalid context" splat:

  BUG: sleeping function called from invalid context at ./include/linux/uaccess.h:169
  in_atomic(): 1, irqs_disabled(): 0, non_block: 0, pid: 1787, name: sudo
  preempt_count: 1, expected: 0
  RCU nest depth: 2, expected: 0

Fix this by rejecting sleepable programs early in
bpf_kprobe_multi_link_attach(), before any further processing.

Fixes: 0dcac2725406 ("bpf: Add multi kprobe link")
Signed-off-by: Varun R Mallya <varunrmallya@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi <memxor@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Leon Hwang <leon.hwang@linux.dev>
Acked-by: Jiri Olsa <jolsa@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260401191126.440683-1-varunrmallya@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

diff --git a/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c b/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
index 0b040a417442..af7079aa0f36 100644
--- a/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
+++ b/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
@@ -2752,6 +2752,10 @@ int bpf_kprobe_multi_link_attach(const union bpf_attr *attr, struct bpf_prog *pr
 	if (!is_kprobe_multi(prog))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	/* kprobe_multi is not allowed to be sleepable. */
+	if (prog->sleepable)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	/* Writing to context is not allowed for kprobes. */
 	if (prog->aux->kprobe_write_ctx)
 		return -EINVAL;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File Modified

**kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c** – In the function `bpf_kprobe_multi_link_attach()`, one validation check was added.

### Modification Details

- **Addition:** An early rejection of sleepable BPF programs.  
  The new check (`if (prog->sleepable) return -EINVAL;`) verifies whether the program has the `sleepable` flag set. If it does, the attachment fails immediately with `-EINVAL`.

- **Placement:** The check is inserted after the initial `is_kprobe_multi(prog)` validation but before the existing `kprobe_write_ctx` check, ensuring that the invalid sleepable property is caught as early as possible.

### Relationship Between Changes

- The single change (addition of a guard clause) directly addresses the root cause of the reported bug: a sleepable program was allowed to attach to a kprobe_multi link, causing a "sleeping function called from invalid context" splat because kprobe_multi handlers run in atomic/RCU context and cannot sleep.

- By rejecting sleepable programs at attach time, the patch prevents the kernel from ever attempting to invoke sleepable helpers (such as `bpf_copy_from_user()`) from the non-sleepable kprobe_multi context, thus eliminating the invalid-context splat.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>if (!is_kprobe_multi(prog))</text>
<text>    return -EINVAL;</text>
<text>/* Missing: check for prog->sleepable */</text>
Reason:
The function `bpf_kprobe_multi_link_attach()` validates the program type but does not check the `sleepable` flag. Since kprobe.multi programs execute in atomic/RCU context, allowing a sleepable program to attach enables the use of sleeping helpers (e.g., `bpf_copy_from_user()`), causing a "sleeping function called from invalid context" splat.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (prog->sleepable)</text>
<text>    return -EINVAL;</text>
Reason:
Adding this early check explicitly rejects any BPF program with the `sleepable` flag set during the attach of a kprobe_multi link. This prevents sleepable helpers from being invoked in atomic context, eliminating the kernel splat.
